name: Achla AI Search
author: achlaai

sections.description:
On a research or documentation site, the visitor almost never uses your exact
term. They ask about protein folding where the page says conformational
dynamics. They use the name their own field gives a method. They type an
acronym that is spelled out on one page and assumed on forty others.

WordPress search matches words. So it returns nothing — while the answer is
sitting on your site.

Achla answers the question instead. Someone asks in their own words, in their
own language, and gets a short answer assembled from your published pages,
with numbered links to every page it drew from.

Free plan: 30 searches a month and 30 indexed pages. No payment card.

What you do not have to set up

Most AI search plugins hand you the hard part. This one does not.

  • No OpenAI or Gemini key. Nothing to sign up for, paste into WordPress,
    keep secret, rotate, or top up.
  • No token bill from a second company. Your plan is counted in searches,
    not in input and output tokens.
  • No search server or vector database. No indexing service to run, size,
    or pay for separately.

Achla does the crawling, the indexing, the model calls, and the updates. You
install the plugin and choose where the widget sits.

Built for sites with more content than anyone can browse

Achla is aimed at sites where the information is deep, technical, and spread
across hundreds of pages:

  • research groups, laboratories, and institutes
  • university departments and faculty sites
  • scientific publications, proceedings, and open archives
  • technical documentation and knowledge bases
  • medical, legal, and regulatory reference sites
  • large catalogs, directories, and databases

It works on a small blog too. It earns its keep on a site nobody can read
end to end.

What visitors get

  • An answer, not another results page. A short response with numbered
    links to the pages that support it.
  • Their own words, not your vocabulary. Synonyms, alternative
    terminology, spelled-out acronyms, and everyday phrasing all reach the same
    page. Visitors do not have to guess your naming.
  • Their own language. Someone writes in Hebrew, French, or Arabic and the
    answer comes back in that language — useful when your readers are
    international and your content is not.
  • Answers anchored in your pages. Achla shows an answer only when it can
    cite supporting pages from your site. If your indexed pages do not provide
    enough support, it says so instead of presenting an unsupported answer.

That last point is the one that matters on a scientific site. A confident
answer with no source is worse than no answer, so Achla will not produce one.

Three ways to place it

  • Bubble — a floating button in the corner. The default; nothing to edit.
  • Inline — a shortcode or a Gutenberg block, anywhere you want it.
  • Attach — hooks onto the search field you already have.

Your existing WordPress search keeps working. Achla sits alongside it.

Getting connected

  1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Click Connect and sign in to Achla. Confirm you own the site. No key is
    copied into WordPress.
  3. Achla reads your public pages and builds the index. WordPress shows you
    the progress.
  4. Pick a placement, preview it, and switch the widget on.

Worth knowing before you install

Written out plainly so nothing surprises you later:

  • An Achla account is required. The free plan does not ask for a card.
  • The free plan stops at 30 searches a month. It does not overspend, and it
    cannot charge you.
  • The free plan indexes 30 pages. On a large site that is enough to try Achla
    on one section — a single lab, one manual, one collection — not to cover
    the whole archive. Point it at the section your visitors ask about most.
  • Answers come only from public pages Achla is allowed to read. Content behind
    a login is not indexed.
  • The widget shows a “Powered by Achla AI” credit.
  • Connecting requires an administrator. Moving the site to a new domain means
    confirming ownership again.
  • On an HTTP site the plugin shows a permanent reduced-security warning. Use
    HTTPS.
  • Colors and styling are set in the Achla dashboard, not in WordPress.

Paid plans start at $15/month and include a fixed number of searches, so you
budget in searches rather than in model tokens.

External services

This plugin requires the third-party Achla AI Search service at
https://achlaai.com. The service crawls permitted public content, builds and
maintains the index, generates cited answers, provides widget configuration,
and manages service billing.

  1. Ownership connection. When an administrator clicks Connect, Resume, or
    Reconnect, the plugin sends the site origin, WordPress callback URL, and a
    short-lived ownership challenge to Achla. The secret verifier is sent only
    after WordPress validates Achla’s signed callback. WordPress then stores the
    site binding, project identifier, public widget key, and a server-side
    management credential.

  2. Lifecycle status and health. While connected, WordPress makes paced,
    authenticated requests to read project and index status. Diagnostics can
    contain only the classified states ATTACH_TARGET_MISSING and
    RELEASE_UNAVAILABLE, software versions, status classifications, and
    timestamps. They do not contain page content, visitor questions, email
    addresses, IP addresses, cookies, secrets, arbitrary URLs, or stack traces.

  3. Disconnect. An administrator disconnect, or uninstall best effort,
    revokes the installation binding and management credential. It does not
    cancel an Achla subscription.

  4. Signed widget release. WordPress periodically requests a signed control
    and manifest from Achla. The connector checks its signature, expiry,
    compatibility, rollback state, immutable asset URL, and Subresource
    Integrity value. The browser loads only a verified release.

  5. Widget use. The verified widget uses Achla’s widget configuration and
    search APIs. When a visitor asks a question, Achla receives the question,
    the site’s public widget key, the page origin, and the visitor’s IP address
    carried by the HTTPS request. These data are used for site binding, abuse
    controls, and returning an answer from the indexed public content.

The plugin’s three public WordPress REST routes are limited to a signed
ownership callback, a no-store release decision, and nonce-protected,
same-origin runtime diagnostics. All management routes require an
administrator capability and WordPress REST nonce.

The local bridge does not use cookies, browser storage, advertising
identifiers, iframes, or page-content telemetry. Review the service terms
before enabling the widget:

  • Privacy Policy: https://achlaai.com/legal/privacy
  • Terms of Service: https://achlaai.com/legal/terms
sections.installation:
1. Install the plugin ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin, or place
    the achlaai directory under /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate Achla AI Search.
  3. Open Settings > Achla AI Search and select Connect.
  4. Complete ownership setup on Achla, then return to WordPress and watch the
    connection and indexing status.
  5. Keep Bubble placement or choose Inline or Attach. Test an Attach selector
    before saving it. Switch “Show the widget” on when you are ready for the
    widget and its Powered by Achla AI credit to be publicly visible.

The widget appears only once the connection is valid, the project is active,
the index is ready, placement is on, and the current signed release passes
verification.
sections.faq:
Is the free plan really free?

Yes. 30 searches a month and 30 indexed pages, with no payment card. It is a
plan, not a trial that expires. When the 30 searches are used up it stops
until the month rolls over — it never quietly charges you for more.

Free projects that sit completely unused are eventually removed, with a
warning by email first.

Do I need my own OpenAI or LLM API key?

No. Achla runs the crawler, the index, and the model calls. There is no key to
obtain, paste into WordPress, secure, rotate, or refill.

Do I have to prepay for tokens?

No. Plans are measured in searches. Paid plans include a fixed allowance, and
extra usage is bought as blocks of searches rather than as model tokens.

Will it make things up?

Achla is designed not to fill gaps with unsupported claims. It shows an answer
only when it can cite pages from your site; when the indexed pages do not
provide enough support, it says so. As with any AI-generated output, visitors
should follow the numbered source links when accuracy matters.

My site has thousands of pages. Can it handle that?

Yes, on a paid plan. The free plan indexes 30 pages, which is meant for
trying Achla on one section rather than covering an archive. Start with the
part of the site visitors ask about most, see whether the answers hold up,
then decide.

Our terminology is specialised. Will it understand the questions?

That is the case Achla is built for. A question is matched against the
meaning of your pages, not their exact wording, so alternative terms, spelled
out acronyms, and plain-language phrasing all reach the right page. Answers
still come only from your content — nothing is imported from outside it.

Can visitors ask in their own language?

Yes. The answer comes back in the language of the question.

Does this replace the WordPress search I already have?

Only if you want it to. Bubble and Inline sit alongside your existing search.
Attach hooks onto your current search field.

What content does it index?

Public pages that Achla is permitted to crawl. Anything behind a login, and
anything your robots rules exclude, stays out.

Does the plugin store visitor data in WordPress?

No. It does not store visitor questions, IP addresses, page content, cookies,
or widget sessions in WordPress. It stores only this site’s connection,
lifecycle, placement, release, and diagnostic state.

The widget is not showing up. Why?

Open Settings > Achla AI Search — the status screen names the reason and the
fix. The usual causes are ownership still needing confirmation, indexing not
finished, placement switched off, or a release that needs to refresh.

What does Attach do if the search field is missing?

Attach accepts a narrow set of CSS selectors and tests them on the server
before saving. If the element is not on the page at runtime, the widget falls
back to Bubble and records a warning, which clears once the field is found
again.

What happens if I deactivate the plugin?

The widget disappears and scheduled work stops. The connection is kept, so
reactivating picks up where it left off. Deactivating does not disconnect the
site and does not cancel a subscription.

What happens if I uninstall it?

Uninstall disconnects the site as far as it can, then removes this site’s
options, temporary connection data, locks, and scheduled hooks. It never
cancels a subscription — cancel that in the Achla dashboard.
sections.changelog:
0.3.5

  • Security hardening: the runtime placement diagnostic endpoint now requires a WordPress nonce issued with the bridge script.

0.3.4

  • Move settings maintenance and public runtime diagnostics to asynchronous scheduled work.
  • Respect lifecycle and release backoff in due-aware status, heartbeat, and release cron callbacks.
  • Enforce signed CMS control expiry when selecting and downloading self-hosted update packages.

0.3.2

  • Keep setup in the current tab so registration and email verification can return to the original WordPress connection.
  • Continue bounded status polling while the first index and signed widget release are being prepared.
  • Improve WordPress.org compatibility checks, release gates, and package metadata.
